correctness.rationale: The graph is diameter two in both budget ranges. Strict variance convexity makes every maximizer an integral three-level potential. Such potentials correspond precisely to crossing complete bicliques in the missing-edge graph, with exact numerator n(a+b)-(a-b)^2. The edge budget forces ab<=k and a+b<=ab+1<=n/2, giving the strict monotone star envelope and equality rigidity; the degree budget forces a,b<=r and the rigid r-by-r biclique. The root and floor convention at the first increase was independently checked with integers, and all claimed boundaries are included.

value.rationale: This is a sharp robustness/classification theorem for the canonical Lipschitz-to-L2 embedding under two natural adversarial edge-loss budgets. The optimal patterns are structurally different (star versus balanced complete biclique), the thresholds are exact and attained, and the new envelopes apply to all admissible graphs rather than selected examples. Their use is to identify when the complete-graph metric constraints cease to determine the sharp variance, a meaningful stability question even without a downstream theorem.
